title: 2027-03-21 hosted API embeddings + rerank demo - NovaSearch
summary: AE + SE walked NovaSearch through Redwood Hosted API embeddings + reranking demo. Covered embedding generation, similarity search, re-rank endpoint, console walkthrough, Optimize recommendations (batching, quantization), and security questions (SOC 2, SSO, VPC options). Agreed to run a small pilot: 2-week benchmark using NovaSearch sample index; Redwood to send pricing, security pack, and benchmark checklist.
topics: Intro & goals: improve search relevance while keeping latency under 120ms
Embeddings endpoint: model choices, vector dim, batching
Rerank endpoint: top-k re-ranking vs full reranking, payload size tradeoffs
Console demo: API keys, routes, cost/latency dashboards, prefix caching
Optimize suggestions: dynamic batching, quantization recommendations, cache TTL
Security: SOC 2, SSO/SAML, KMS encryption, VPC/private deployments
Next steps: pilot, pricing, security docs
action_items: Ava - send pilot pricing sheet + example contract (by 2027-03-23)
Jon - share benchmark checklist and sample curl scripts (by 2027-03-22)
Priya - provide sample dataset (search queries + click labels) for pilot (by 2027-03-25)
Tom - schedule 30m follow-up with infra team to discuss VPC details (by 2027-03-24)
next_steps: Redwood to provision trial API key and shared workspace for NovaSearch
Run 2-week pilot: NovaSearch to run relevance benchmarks; Redwood to assist with scripts
Follow-up call to review pilot results and pricing (tentative week of 2027-04-05)
meeting_header: Date/Time: 2027-03-21 09:00 PDT | Duration: 49 minutes | Attendees: Ava Martinez (Redwood AE), Jon Park (Redwood SE), Priya Singh (NovaSearch Head of Search), Tom Reynolds (NovaSearch Eng Manager), Lian Zhao (NovaSearch ML Eng)
transcript: 00:00 Ava: hey everyone thanks for joining, um we wanted to show a quick walkthrough of the hosted API for embeddings and the rerank endpoint, and then go into how Optimize can help lower cost without hurting relevance. 00:12 Priya: perfect thanks Ava, our goal is to improve our search relevance for product search and keep p95 under ~120ms if possible. 00:20 Jon: yep for context i'll lead the demo portion, Ava will cover pilot and commercial stuff. 00:28 Tom: quick note, infra will want VPC options and audit logs, also SSO is a must. 00:35 Ava: totally noted, we'll cover security later in the call. 01:02 Jon: ok starting with embeddings, Redwood's hosted embeddings endpoint supports multiple models, default sizes are 768 and 1536 dims, we usually recommend the 1536 for commerce catalogs because you get better sem-sim accuracy. 01:20 Lian: how do you handle batching? we have bursts of indexing traffic during deploys. 01:28 Jon: we do continuous batching in the runtime; the hosted API auto-batches requests up to a latency SLA you set, you can tune max_batch_size and latency_target. that helps throughput without large latency spikes. 01:45 Priya: any quantization options for hosted? we want to control cost. 01:52 Jon: hosted supports quantized model variants under the hood — Optimize will recommend the quantization profile per workload; for embeddings it's often fp16 or int8-like quant for vectors which reduces cost with minimal quality loss. 02:12 Tom: curious about where people store vectors, are you expecting us to use pinecone/algolia or do you have a vector store? 02:20 Jon: Redwood doesn't force a store — you can keep vectors in whatever you use; we integrate well with Pinecone and you can push embeddings to Algolia or OpenSearch. for the rerank step we fetch top-k from your store then call Redwood rerank endpoint with those candidates. 02:42 Priya: can you show the rerank API flow? 02:46 Jon: yup — quick curl example: curl -X POST /v1/rerank -d '{"query":"user query","candidates":[{"id":"123","text":"..."}, ...] }' header Authorization: Bearer KEY — response returns ranked candidates and scores. note that you can pass embeddings instead of raw text to reduce tokenization cost. 03:10 Priya: interesting, how big should top-k be? we currently return top-100 from ES then rerank. 03:18 Jon: typically top-10 to top-50 is the sweet spot — top-100 is ok but cost and latency rise linearly. we showed a benchmark where top-20 rerank gave 95% of the gain of top-100 but at half the cost. 03:35 Lian: are there options to do partial rerank / hybrid? 03:40 Jon: yes hybrid approaches: use similarity scores to filter to a smaller set then rerank; or use a cheap lightweight model first and then a heavier model for final rerank. 03:54 Ava: moving to the console quick — i'll share my screen (note: link to deck shared in chat). 04:05 Ava: on the console you can create routes: embeddings-route, rerank-route, set model version pinning, and see token-level cost and latency per route. you can also set rollouts: canary or A/B. 04:25 Priya: can we see historical latency per key? 04:28 Jon: yes the console has per-key and per-route dashboards, you can slice by model and region. 04:40 Tom: about caching — do you do prefix/KV caching for rerank? 04:46 Jon: we do prefix and KV caching for generation workloads; for rerank we cache candidate embeddings and intermediate KV where useful. caching TTLs are adjustable. 05:05 Priya: what about data retention and logs? compliance folks will ask. 05:10 Ava: Redwood offers audit logs, configurable retention; for Private deployments we can do customer-managed KMS/HSM and on-prem if needed. hosted has SOC 2 compliance — full pack available. 05:28 Tom: SSO and RBAC? 05:31 Ava: yes, SSO via SAML/Okta, SCIM for user provisioning, role-based access controls in console. we'll send the security pack after call. 05:44 Priya: good. 06:05 Jon: back to rerank details — scoring: we return a score for each candidate; you can select argmax or sample, and we also provide calibrated confidence if you ask for it. 06:20 Lian: calibration? can you explain quickly — we want to know how to threshold results. 06:26 Jon: calibration is basically mapping raw logits to probabilities; we surface a score field and you can apply thresholds in your app layer. 06:40 Priya: any limits on payload size for rerank? we have long product descriptions. 06:45 Jon: payloads up to ~256KB per request for hosted is supported, beyond that we recommend passing embeddings or truncating descriptions. 07:00 Tom: latency numbers — what p95 should we expect for rerank top-20? 07:06 Jon: hosted typical p95 for rerank top-20 with 1536-d vectors is around 80-140ms depending on region and load; we can aim to keep yours under 120ms with the right routing and batching. 07:24 Priya: cost estimates? 07:27 Ava: we'll send a pricing example in the follow-up, but rough rule: embedding cost per vector + rerank per candidate token cost. Optimize can dial down cost via recommended batching, model variant selection, and KV caching. 07:46 Lian: demo time — show the live endpoint hitting our small dataset. 07:50 Jon: hitting it now — (typing sound) 08:05 Jon: ok sent a query "red shoes size 9" — backend returns top-50 from store, we rerank top-20, here's the JSON response, note the scores and id ordering. 08:25 Priya: wow the reorder looks right on first glance. 08:30 Tom: can we see an example of passing embeddings instead of text? 08:34 Jon: sure — here's curl to call /v1/embeddings then send vectors in rerank payload, reduces tokenization. 08:50 Priya: what about model drift monitoring? we have seasonal catalogs. 08:55 Jon: Optimize includes quality monitoring tied to prompt sets and evals; you can upload a set of queries+relevance labels, Redwood runs regression checks on new model versions and alerts. 09:10 Priya: that helps. 09:20 Tom: about private deployments — we might need an on-prem option for EU customers. 09:26 Ava: Private supports VPC and on-prem packages; there is a platform fee + support tier. for sensitive EU data we can set up a dedicated region or private deployment. 09:40 Priya: what's the SLAs for Dedicated vs Hosted? 09:44 Jon: Dedicated gives SLA-backed latency and uptime; hosted has best-effort but strong SLOs for most customers. Dedicated is recommended when you need strict p99 latency guarantees and isolation. 10:05 Priya: ok what's needed to start a pilot? 10:09 Ava: minimal: sample dataset, definition of success metrics, a POC contact, and agreement on timescale — we'll run a 2-week pilot. 10:20 Priya: timeline: we want results before end of month. 10:24 Ava: sounds feasible. 10:30 Jon: quick note on integration: client libraries available in python/node, and the API is simple REST or gRPC for streaming where relevant. 10:43 Lian: are there any gotchas with tokenization differences across model versions? 10:48 Jon: small differences exist; Optimize's eval harness can run side-by-side tokenization checks. 11:05 Tom: procurement questions — do you have standard enterprise T&Cs? 11:09 Ava: yes we have a standard contract and can fast-track with procurement if you sign up for Dedicated. 11:20 Priya: competitor question — how does this compare to using Algolia + custom re-ranker? 11:26 Jon: Algolia is great for fast retrieval but you're limited in model-based re-ranking; Redwood pairs with stores and provides model-backed reranking with observability and unit cost controls. 11:42 Tom: any reference customers in commerce? 11:45 Ava: we can share a brief case study; i'll attach in follow-up. 12:02 Jon: demo wrap — performance note: use top-k curation, dynamic batching, and quantization from Optimize to reduce unit cost by up to ~40% depending on workload. 12:18 Priya: this looks promising, let's kick off pilot. 12:22 Ava: recap of next steps: we'll send pricing, security docs, provide trial keys, and benchmark checklist. 12:30 Priya: thanks all. 48:50 Ava: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in the chat with links and next steps.
